themes.youtube_title: Why Deep-Sea Hulls IMPLODE in Milliseconds
themes.frame_0_visual_concept: Isometric 2.5D pressure-hull cutaway ringed by dense glowing cyan and crimson inward hydrostatic force arrows under a deep-navy volumetric spotlight at t=0.0s.
themes.core_physics: Hydrostatic water pressure increases roughly 1 atmosphere every 10 meters, reaching ~380 atmospheres (~400 tons per square foot) at 3,800 meters. Deep-ocean submersibles use isotropic titanium spheres because spherical geometry distributes compressive stress evenly. By contrast, carbon-fiber composite cylinders bonded to titanium end-rings excel in tension but suffer cyclic compressive micro-delamination between resin plies; once a tiny geometric dimple forms, elastic buckling collapses the hull in ~20 milliseconds — over 10x faster than a ~250ms human visual nerve signal — while water rushes inward faster than a jetliner.

themes.youtube_title: Why Light Wind RIPPED This Steel Bridge Apart
themes.frame_0_visual_concept: Isometric 2.5D suspension bridge deck twisting in violent sinusoidal torsion with glowing cyan airflow ribbons curling into crimson vortices at t=0.0s.
themes.core_physics: Contrary to the textbook simple-resonance myth, the 1940 suspension bridge collapse was driven by aeroelastic flutter: solid 8-foot H-shaped plate girders blocked steady 42 mph wind, shedding alternating vortices that fed energy into the deck's torsional twist (negative aerodynamic damping) until vertical suspender cables exceeded tensile yield and snapped in sequence. Modern long-span bridges prevent flutter with streamlined aerodynamic box girders and open wind slots.

themes.youtube_title: The Genius Gear That Lets Cars TURN Smoothly
themes.frame_0_visual_concept: Gleaming 2.5D isometric brass-and-steel bevel differential gear cage meshing in motion with glowing amber torque streams splitting unevenly left and right at t=0.0s.
themes.core_physics: Around any curve, the outer tire travels a longer arc than the inner tire. An open mechanical differential uses a ring-and-pinion carrier holding orbiting bevel spider gears meshed with left and right axle side gears: driving straight, spider gears ride stationary on their pin; cornering, they spin on their axis to subtract RPM from the inner wheel and add equal RPM to the outer wheel — while revealing why one tire on ice steals all traction unless limited-slip clutches intervene.

themes.youtube_title: How One Tiny Bolt Change DOUBLED Steel Stress
themes.frame_0_visual_concept: High-contrast 2.5D isometric cutaway of a single hexagonal steel nut pressing down on a glowing crimson overloaded welded box-beam flange at t=0.0s.
themes.core_physics: Classic textbook statics failure: two stacked suspended atrium walkways were originally specified on a single continuous vertical hanger rod carrying 1W on the upper nut and 1W on the lower nut. Changing to two offset rods for easier assembly hung the lower walkway directly from the upper box beam, channeling 2W (200% bearing and weld shear stress) onto the upper nut until the thin box-beam seam peeled open and pulled through.
